FormHypes · proposed research protocol · 16 October 2026

By Dr Non · depa + Axiom · inspired by Shouheng Chen (陈寿恒)

Study status: protocol and working prototype; no participant, leasing or willingness-to-pay results collected.

A paid comparison is still a hypothesis.

Commercial hypotheses · no sales or adoption results claimed

The plausible first product is a concept-comparison service for architects and development teams. Give a team a fixed brief, make several forms comparable, and show what changes in usable area, envelope and the stated income scenario. The paid deliverable could be a documented shortlist with editable geometry and assumptions. This is a business hypothesis.

“Best form” needs a context. A corner-rich plan may lose usable area around a large core. A compact envelope may cost less to maintain. A skyline gesture may need a client’s willingness to pay, while a neighbour may ask for less shadow. Show the alternatives and the reason for the choice; a single score cannot settle every stakeholder’s question. Landlord yield and the other reasons to build are FormHypes scenarios from 2026. They are not chapters of Chen’s thesis, which embedded how a tower is made.

Start with a paid, bounded feasibility comparison. If teams reuse it and the evidence supports it, test a practice subscription or a professional integration. Pricing, procurement costs and the size of the market remain unmeasured. A credible probability of commercial success needs pilot data; this instrument does not invent a percentage.

Potential buyer | Output worth testing | Evidence of value

Architecture practice | Same-brief alternatives with model and assumption exports | Less preparation time with no loss of review quality

Developer / asset team | A transparent shortlist and sensitivity record | A changed decision with independently checked costs and rents

Public or institutional client | Trade-offs between private income and public effects | Stakeholders can understand and contest the assumptions

Keep the area fixed. Change the form. Then test the claim.

Reproducible scenario + proposed external evaluation

The live table below runs three plan families against your current Studio assumptions. Each is resized to the same gross floor area. It reports corner share, envelope and annual contribution, including failed model constraints. Changing the Studio inputs changes these results. This is a reproducible model experiment, not a market finding.

The first proposed study compares the same architectural task in a conventional workflow and FormHypes. Counterbalance the task order, record elapsed time and corrections, and ask independent architects to review anonymised outputs. Publish the brief, model version, participant criteria and evaluation rubric before collecting outcomes.

A second study tests the income assumptions against permissioned, anonymised leasing and cost evidence. Keep a held-out set of buildings; account for location, age, quality and lease terms before associating form with rent. A third study uses site walks, stakeholder interviews and shadow scenarios to investigate iconicity and public effects. Report disagreement and uncertainty alongside any average result.

Hypothesis | Measurement | What would weaken the claim?

The tool saves useful design time | Time to reviewed alternatives; error and correction rates | Faster output with more errors or poorer review quality

Form changes financial performance | Held-out rental/cost comparisons and sensitivity ranges | The apparent benefit disappears after contextual controls

The comparison supports public discussion | Participant understanding, contested assumptions and access concerns | A convincing image hides harms or excludes affected people

From embedded design knowledge to situated value.

Proposed paper · research protocol, not published findings

Proposed abstract. Chen’s 2006 MIT thesis embedded how a tower is made. Early CAD forced the architect to repeat the work; the expertise was not in the tool. He took massing and detail conventions from practice — HKIFC, Petronas, Cira and Hearst, curtain wall and diagrid — and encoded them. Profile Finding and Point Finding reconstruct a known tower, then transform it. FormHypes is Dr Non’s later instrument, a twentieth-anniversary gift to Shouheng Chen (Xiaohei), and it asks a different question: when does form create inspectable value, and for whom? Value here is not one score. The 2006 thesis did not solve rent, NOI or structure. Studio’s figures are 2026 scenarios that Non owns. They are not Chen’s results. This chapter is a research protocol, not a published finding and not his PDF. (Shouheng Chen, 2006) (Non Arkaraprasertkul, 2007) (Non Arkaraprasertkul, 2008) (Non Arkaraprasertkul, 2016)

Method. The working evidence is a browser prototype on one geometry path. Conservation tests check area accounting. Equal-area comparison holds gross floor area and changes the plan: fix the area, change the form, read what moved. That is Chen’s chapter 5 ritual in this instrument. Corners, envelope and shadow stay assumptions you can inspect. Shenzhen enters as the published storeys, height and gross area of one pilot building, read beside this model’s plot and floor-area ratio. It is context, not proof. Timed tasks, held-out leasing checks and stakeholder studies have not been run. Computed scenarios stay separate from observations collected later. The prototype does not certify structure, carbon or ecology. (Shouheng Chen, 2006)

What would make the argument publishable is the evaluation still ahead: whether reusable rules make an early decision clearer, where the income scenario fails once location and lease terms are controlled, and whose values remain visible. Archive the code revision, inputs, consent and the limits Chen already named — work behind the skin, structural and ecological performance, and a test in live practice. State who built the system and who evaluated it. An inspiration credit is not research authorship. The next step is that evidence, not a sales claim.

Paper section | What belongs in it

Introduction and related work | Chen’s computational methods; Non’s urban inquiry; contemporary design tools

System and provenance | Geometry, data contracts, source reading scope and implementation boundaries

Evaluation | Counterbalanced workflow tasks, held-out market checks, situated fieldwork

Results | Computed scenarios now; measured findings only after the studies

Discussion and limitations | Model sensitivity, selection effects, ground/engineering gaps and distribution of benefits

Reproducibility and contributions | Versioned protocol, lawful data access, author roles and acknowledgements
